charset #

The file's character encoding. The EditorConfig specification enumerates the domain: “Set to latin1, utf-8, utf-8-bom, utf-16be or utf-16le to control the character set.” ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified not a formatter option. Probed at utf-8, utf-8-bom, latin1 and utf-16le on a file carrying non-ASCII text, comparing raw bytes rather than normalised text: the oracle returned the same bytes at all four, adding no BOM and re-encoding nothing, and so did Skala. Neither engine re-encodes, so no oracle fixture can pin this key.

end_of_line #

The line ending written by the formatter. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified masked. ⚠ Masked by skala_enforce_line_ending_style = false, and the mask is section-ordered in a way that defeats the sweep's own override mechanism. With the export as written, a CRLF fixture comes back CRLF from both engines. Appending end_of_line = lf in a later [*.cs] section — exactly what a key flip does — makes the oracle convert to LF, because the later section outranks the earlier enforce_line_ending_style = false; add enforce_line_ending_style = false to that same appended section and CRLF returns. So a one-key flip measures a configuration the standard never has: the oracle gives three distinct outputs at lf/crlf/cr, Skala one, and the glob would report INERT for a divergence that does not exist at the export's own value. Held at enforce_line_ending_style = true, both engines distinguish lf from crlf and agree — the key is read on both sides.

Typeone of lf, crlf, cr
Defaultlf

skala_remove_spaces_on_blank_lines #

Undocumented ReSharper property; classified as C#-relevant by vocabulary. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified implementable — the oracle honours it and Skala does not. ⚠ Refines the recorded OfInert reason. Compared raw, the oracle gives two distinct outputs: at the export's true it strips the spaces from a blank line, and at false it keeps them. Skala strips at both values, so it agrees at the standard and diverges away from it. The reason it cannot follow is structural — its writer emits a blank line as a break followed by a break with nothing between them — and an oracle glob would report INERT. The committed constructs/file/skala_remove_spaces_on_blank_lines.cs cannot exercise the key either way: its blank line carries no spaces.

Typetrue / false
Defaulttrue
Default known fromnothing beyond the export
TierD — recorded so the key is not reported unknown; nothing reads it yet

trim_trailing_whitespace #

Whether trailing whitespace is removed from every line. ⚠ jb cleanupcode ignores it: probed with = true on a doc comment carrying a trailing space, the oracle returns the space. Skala matches the oracle rather than the key, so it is inert in both directions. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified not a formatter option. Probed raw at both values on a fixture carrying trailing spaces after a statement, inside a // comment, and on two blank lines: identical bytes from both engines. The positive control is the same fixture — skala_remove_spaces_on_blank_lines moves the oracle there — so the flatness is the key's and not the fixture's. jb cleanupcode ignores this key, and the recorded oracle-probe default is confirmed.
